findings.summary: Local isPublished() omits the DEV bypass that data-utils.ts's isPublished() has, despite the comment claiming to mirror it.
findings.mechanism: data-utils.ts's isPublished() short-circuits the future-date check with `import.meta.env.DEV`, so in `pnpm dev` a non-draft, future-dated post is still listed and its page is built/reachable. This plugin's isPublished() (line 32-37) has no such bypass, so during dev it still strips/downgrades any inbound link to that same future-dated post to plain text — even though the target page is live and appears in listings. The comment at line ~9 explicitly says 'Mirrors apps/web/src/utils/data-utils.ts', but the mirror is incomplete, producing dev-only inconsistency between what's linked and what's actually published/listed.

findings.summary: A link to a nonexistent slug (typo, renamed/removed post) is silently downgraded exactly like a legitimately-unpublished post.
findings.mechanism: `articles.get(match[1])` returns undefined for any `/blog/<slug>` link whose slug isn't in the articles directory (e.g. a typo or a post that was renamed/deleted). `isPublished(undefined)` returns false (line 33: `if (!article) return false`), so the link is stripped and merged into the generic 'unpublished post(s)' warning, indistinguishable from a real scheduling case. This converts what should be a build-visible broken-link error into an easy-to-miss log line, silently masking authoring mistakes.
